problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={t}^{2}+2,\,y={t}^{4}+{t}^{2}.$ Given  that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2{t}^{2}+1,$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve Given the First Derivative
examples.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x =e^{t}, \, y= e^{2t}+1.$ Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 2e^t,$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 2e^t,$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows:

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} (e^t) = e^t
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2{e}^{t})}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{t}}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
